title: Mentoring and development plans for developers

videos.script: Diego joined the checkout team eight months ago. He writes careful code and asks very few questions. In June he asks Lívia to mentor him. {{title}} Most senior engineers answer that by giving advice. Telling is fast, and it feels like helping. {{roles}} This lesson separates three things that all get called mentoring. Advising from experience. Asking until the other person finds their own answer. And putting their name forward in rooms they are not in. {{three}} Then the first conversation, in four steps: what he wants, where he is, what he could do, and what he will do. {{grow}} A plan with one goal and the evidence that would show it. Work that stretches him, with a net. {{zone}} And an ending, chosen on purpose, with the goal met.
